A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TIPA/MTIPA work. All 14 pages of v1 and 17 pages of v4, including Appendix A, are readable, and the retained methods, experiments, tables and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original Chinese spelling-correction experiments, forward/reverse training comparisons, training dynamics and output analyses in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds comparator evaluations, 1.5B-model experiments, and general and multilingual evaluations of a TIPA-trained Llama model.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 adds full-parameter instruction fine-tuning with TIPA and Tulu-3 data alongside the original LoRA-based CSC training. This extends the parameter-update procedure, while the reverse-position targets, optional pruning and TIPA/MTIPA algorithms remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v4 retains Wang271K, CSCD-NS and LEMON, and adds Tulu-3 instruction training plus IFEVAL, GSM8K, MMLU, AExams, KoBEST, HumanEval and TyDi QA evaluation. It also introduces multilingual occurrence-counting, length-prediction and distinct-character tasks, substantially broadening coverage beyond Chinese spelling correction.

E2.justification: v4 Table 4 adds DeepSeek v2.5, GLM-4-Plus and ERNIE-4.0 to the position-aware CSC comparison in v1 Table 1. The new general-model experiments also introduce Llama-3.1-Tulu as the comparator for Tulu-TIPA. The original CSC comparators remain.

E3.justification: v4 adds a Llama-3.1-8B full-parameter training protocol with two epochs and batch size 32, and extends CSC evaluation to 1.5B models. New benchmark protocols include zero-shot IFEVAL, eight-shot GSM8K and five-shot MMLU. The previously reported CSC splits and training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: v4 adds an output-token efficiency comparison between traditional and position-based CSC in Table 3, and extends forward/reverse and output-length analyses to 1.5B models. Earlier position-wise analyses, training curves and qualitative examples remain; the loss analysis moves to Appendix A.7.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, variability estimates or significance tests. The additional v4 tables continue reporting point estimates; averages across languages or domains do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Matched existing CSC scores are unchanged, but v4 adds substantial results for new comparators, 1.5B models, output-token counts and general-model evaluations. Within the new v4 experiment, TULU/TULU-TIPA achieve TyDi QA averages of 47.85/52.81 and distinct-character scores of 9.29/18.74, while HumanEval falls from 53.05 to 51.83.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 rewrites the PPA numerator from a set of correctly matched prediction pairs to a set of equality expressions. The surrounding prose retains the original intended metric, creating a local formal ambiguity. Equations 1-3 and the reverse-position construction remain unchanged, with no new proofs.

C1.justification: v4 broadens the headline contributions from CSC improvements to multilingual capabilities, general-model performance preservation and full-parameter training, while emphasizing shorter correction outputs. Its conclusion also attributes a 5.64-point F1 gain to traditional CSC, although that gain belongs to the position-aware experiment in Table 4.

C2.justification: v4 replaces the Chinese-only evaluation limitation with a warning that excessive TIPA mixing can bias generation toward shorter outputs. It adds discussion of MTIPA training cost and possible LoRA task interference, qualifies cross-tokenizer comparisons, and interprets the new evaluations as evidence of broader transfer. The OOV limitation remains.

D1.justification: v4 supplies an explicit TIPA prompt, detailed pruning and dataset-mixing procedures, full-parameter hardware/hyperparameters/runtime, and 1.5B resource figures. It newly documents exclusion of unequal-length model outputs and half-/full-width character normalization; these disclosures do not establish changes to the earlier experiments. Construction details for the new character-task datasets remain limited.

R1.justification: Related work adds targeted contrasts with ByT5, CANINE and Itzhak and Levy's explicit-spelling study, alongside citations supporting the new models and benchmarks. Some foundational GPT references are removed. These refine the existing positioning around architecture-preserving character-position training.

P1.justification: v4 substantially rewrites the abstract, condenses the introduction and related work, and recasts the contributions and conclusion. The narrative expands from two experiments to three, implementation details gain dedicated subsections, and the loss discussion moves from the main analysis to the appendix.

P2.justification: v4 redraws Figures 1-2, restyles existing plots, expands CSC tables and adds explanatory and general-evaluation tables. v1's token-length Table 11 becomes a logarithmic bar chart in v4 Figure 5, while the retained loss plot moves to the appendix as Figure 6.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially addresses v1's explicit restriction to Chinese CSC through a second model family, full-parameter training, multilingual QA and direct character-task evaluations, supported by better training documentation. This materially strengthens evidence about generality. The new character datasets remain underdocumented, and the conclusion overstates benchmark preservation and misattributes the 5.64-point gain, but these reporting weaknesses do not outweigh the substantial validation gains.
